title: Root launcher tarball digest matches linux/win32 qualification reports but not darwin (0.8.0 and 0.9.0)
description: Found verifying LCLI-567 on 2026-09-22: the published @opum-ai/lore root tarball's sha256 equals rootTarballSha256 in the four linux/win32 ladybug-package-qualification reports of Release runs 35409381009 (0.8.0) and 35794336818 (0.9.0), and differs from the two darwin reports. scripts/publish-release.sh treats the launcher as locally self-sealed because nothing independent records its digest; if rootTarballSha256 IS such a record on some hosts, the launcher could be independently verified -- but only once it is understood what that field measures per host and why darwin differs (packing on the host? mtime? tar flavour?). Evidence: scratchpad verify/ dir of the LCLI-567 session. Do not assume either reading.

acceptanceCriteria.text: What rootTarballSha256 measures on each host is established from release.yml and the qualification script, not inferred
The darwin/linux divergence is explained by a named mechanism, reproduced
Decide (with evidence) whether publish-release.sh can verify the launcher against a CI record, and either implement it or record why not

implementationNotes: Carried in the 2026-09-22 recycle handoff (LCLI-569 item 1); nobody has started it. Evidence dir (session scratchpad verify/) does not survive the recycle -- re-derive from Release runs 35409381009 and 35794336818's ladybug-package-qualification artifacts and the registry tarballs.

Third release with the same split, 0.9.1 (Release run 35953824422, 2026-09-24). The registry's @opum-ai/lore@0.9.1 tarball hashes to 45f7c5f3..., which equals rootTarballSha256 in the linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-arm64 and win32-x64 reports and the script's self-seal. Both darwin reports record b1361383.... All six platform tarballs match their reports. Mechanism still unestablished.

AC1 (from source, read on dev 7e5ca28a): rootTarballSha256 is sha256File of the root tarball that EACH matching-host package-qualification job packs ITSELF: benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts stages the root package, then runs 'npm pack --pack-destination artifactRoot' (about line 313) and records sha256File(rootTarball) (line 455). It is not a digest of the npm-packages artifact, which the separate 'package' job packs on ubuntu-24.04. release.yml's package-qualification job has no setup-node step, so each host packs with its runner image's preinstalled node/npm. The reports record no node, npm or zlib version: key set checked, only platform.node exists.

AC2 (reproduced 2026-09-25 on lore 0.9.3, Release run 36088480940, from the downloaded ladybug-package-qualification-<host> artifacts, which include the host-packed tarballs). The root tarballs from the darwin-arm64 and darwin-x64 runners are d2231359..., 10987 bytes. linux-x64, win32-x64 and npm-packages are c70fd8db..., 11008 bytes. All have the IDENTICAL 10-byte gzip header 1f8b08000000000002ff (mtime 0, XFL 2, OS 0xff from node-tar portable mode) and an IDENTICAL decompressed tar stream (576c6341...). Only the deflate stream differs, so this is not mtime, content, header or tar flavour. MECHANISM: macOS's SYSTEM zlib (stock zlib 1.2.12, via /usr/bin/python3's zlib) at level 9 on that tar stream, with the header normalised to node-tar's, reproduces d2231359 BYTE-IDENTICALLY, deflate and trailer included (cmp clean). Node's BUNDLED zlib (Chromium fork, 'motley'/e00f703) reproduces c70fd8db on this Mac under node v20.20.2, v22.23.3 and v24.20.0 alike. So neither the OS nor the Node major is the variable. The zlib implementation is. INFERRED, NOT MEASURED: that the darwin runner images' node links the shared system zlib rather than the bundled copy (Homebrew-style --shared-zlib). Confirm by printing process.versions.zlib in the darwin package-qualification job; the runner logs do not record it. Consistent with 0.8.0, 0.9.0 and 0.9.1 all showing the same OS-split.

AC3 DECISION: do NOT verify the root launcher against rootTarballSha256 in publish-release.sh. (a) The field measures whichever zlib the runner image's node happens to link, so the four linux/win32 reports agree with npm-packages only by coincidence of image contents, and darwin never does. A check keyed on it would go red on an unrelated runner-image change. (b) The gap it would have closed is closed already: since LCLI-578 (opum-ai/lore-cli#269), publish-release.sh refuses unless opum-cli-e2e's receipt names all seven tarball sha256s, root included. That is a digest recorded by another repository, and it was measured live on 0.9.3: a re-gzipped root with an identical tar stream was refused. If a CI-side root record is ever wanted, the robust form is to record the UNCOMPRESSED tar-stream sha256 (compression-independent), or to pin setup-node in package-qualification. Neither is filed, because the receipt covers the need. FOLLOW-ON: the script header (publish-release.sh:77-79) and runbook (release-publishing.md:696) still say the root launcher's digest is 'recorded nowhere' and 'irreducibly a self-seal', which is stale since LCLI-578. Noted on LCLI-586, which already reworks root-tarball handling in that file.
finalSummary: Investigation only; no code change. The darwin/linux split in rootTarballSha256 comes from the COMPRESSOR, not the content. Each qualification host npm-packs the root launcher itself, with its runner image's node, and the darwin runners' gzip output matches macOS's stock system zlib 1.2.12 at level 9 byte-for-byte. linux/win32 and npm-packages match Node's bundled Chromium-fork zlib, which I reproduced on node 20, 22 and 24. Identical gzip headers and an identical tar stream across all hosts were confirmed on 0.9.3's real artifacts (Release run 36088480940). The one inferred link, that the darwin runner's node links the shared system zlib, is named with how to confirm it. Decision: publish-release.sh will not verify the launcher against that field, because it is runner-image-dependent. The need is already met by LCLI-578's receipt gate (opum-ai/lore-cli#269), which binds the root digest from another repository. Stale 'recorded nowhere' prose is noted on LCLI-586.
